description:
Issue summary: Customers (NovusDocs, dedicated cluster) saw a sharp rise in 5xx responses from the hosted API between 2026-03-10T10:12Z and 2026-03-10T10:42Z. Errors were primarily 502/503 returned by the API gateway. Concurrently, several serving-runtime GPU processes on the affected nodes experienced watchdog-triggered restarts (NVML reset noted). Impact: Intermittent request failures for customer traffic (~8-12% error rate for the tenant during the window), higher tail latency for long-running streaming sessions, and several failed batch embedding uploads. Environment: prod, us-east-1, dedicated pool for NovusDocs. Severity: Sev1 affecting production traffic.

High-level hypothesis: A spike of short-lived connections and SDK keepalive churn from a customer-side client version produced a handshake/backlog in our ephemeral proxy layer, which caused accept/handshake stalls. Stalled handshakes prevented timely request handoff to the serving-runtime, producing cascading timeouts and retries at the gateway. The serving runtime experienced a sudden increase in prefetch concurrency and small-batch fanout which pushed GPUs into a thrash pattern (frequent small kernels + repeated memory allocations), provoking NVML driver resets and runtime watchdog restarts.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use the NovusDocs client SDK v1.12 with default keepalive (10s) and aggressive reconnect on 5xx.
2) Simulate burst of ~1800 short requests/min with many <200 token prompts and interleaved streaming sessions.
3) Observe the ephemeral proxy handshake queue growth at the proxy layer, then watch API gateway 502/503 responses and serving-runtime NVML reset logs.

Note: reproducer uses traffic shape and SDK behavior aligned with customer telemetry; simple long-lived steady traffic does not reproduce the failure pattern.
logs:
api-gateway: 2026-03-10T10:13:01Z WARN accept_queue_len=512 handshake_latency_ms_p95=4200 returning=502 tenant=novusdocs
ephemeral-proxy: 2026-03-10T10:13:02Z ERROR tls_handshake_timeout conn_id=0x7f8c queue_len=498
serving-runtime: 2026-03-10T10:13:05Z ERROR nvml: GPU 0 reset detected (reason: driver-reset) pid=2418
serving-runtime: 2026-03-10T10:13:05Z INFO watchdog: restart triggered (runtime-id=rt-1132)
proxy-metrics: handshake_backlog{region="us-east-1"} 482 at 2026-03-10T10:14:00Z
customer-sdk (NovusDocs v1.12): reconnect_immediate_on_5xx=true keepalive=10s
investigation_notes:
Initial triage (support): validated customer error spikes via tenant metrics and confirmed 5xx wave correlated to NovusDocs traffic. Eng (ingress/proxy) looked at handshake queue and found prolonged TLS handshake latency. Observed unusually high number of TCP half-open connections and short-lived connection churn. Runtime team observed GPU NVML resets coincident with the same time window; crash dumps show repeated small-kernel churn and rapid allocator/free cycles.

Key findings so far:
- Ephemeral proxy accept queue growth correlates with SDK reconnect behavior documented in NovusDocs support bundle.
- Proxy CPU was not saturated; contention appears in accept/handshake worker pools and downstream channel handoff.
- Serving runtime experienced increased small-batch scheduling overhead leading to elevated GPU utilization with many sub-10ms kernels, which is known to increase driver stress on certain NVidia driver versions.
- Customer traffic shape and client reconnect policy amplified the effect (retry-on-5xx immediate).

Open questions:
- Does the customer's SDK change between v1.11 and v1.12 explain rate of reconnects? (CS to confirm).
- Can we throttle or coalesce handshake processing at the proxy without impacting latency SLAs?
- Is there a kernel scheduling change we can make in serving-runtime to reduce allocator churn during small-batch fanouts?
resolution_notes:
Mitigations implemented (temporary):
- Applied a targeted rate-limit on new connection accepts for the NovusDocs tenant at the proxy layer (soft 40 conn/s cap) to smooth handshake bursts.
- Backfilled a proxy worker pool patch to increase handshake worker count and to prioritize handoff fairness for pinned tenants.
- Rolled out a hotfix to the serving-runtime to coalesce tiny prefetch kernels into micro-batches (v2.7.3-hotfix) for the affected dedicated pool.
- Asked NovusDocs to roll client to v1.13 (patched to exponential backoff on 5xx and keepalive jitter).

Outcome: error rate reduced to baseline (~0.3% tenant error rate) within 20 minutes of mitigations. No further NVML resets observed after runtime hotfix rollout.

Follow-up actions (owners):
- SRE: monitor handshake_backlog and implement alert threshold (owner: Carlos Mendes).
- Runtime: evaluate micro-batch coalescing for general release and benchmark driver stability across NVidia driver versions (owner: Linh Tran).
- Support/CS: coordinate with NovusDocs on client rollout and request replay of traffic window for SDK team (owner: Maya Singh).
- Product: consider adding tenant-level handshake smoothing policy as a control plane config (owner: Priya Rao).
